outcome: Mode of delivery (vaginal vs. cesarean section)
Neonatal complications (pneumonia, respiratory distress syndrome, neonatal sepsis, hypoglycemia)
cohort: The study included 126 pregnant women at term (37-40 weeks) with confirmed premature rupture of membranes (PROM), singleton cephalic pregnancies, adequate pelvis, and no history of previous uterine surgery, non-cephalic presentation, intrauterine growth restriction, or maternal hypertensive/diabetic disorders.
finding: Low amniotic fluid index (AFI < 5 cm) in term PROM cases was significantly associated with higher cesarean section rates, primarily due to fetal distress and failed induction, and an increased incidence of neonatal complications.
mod_finding: Women with low AFI (< 5 cm) had significantly lower rates of vaginal delivery (10% vs 65.8%) and successful vaginal delivery after induction (25% vs 77.8%) compared to those with AFI ≥ 5 cm, resulting in significantly higher cesarean section rates (90% vs 34.2%).
